approachQuestion.prompt:
Reordered Badge Occurrences

A lowercase string `log` records letter badges in order. A non-empty lowercase string `badge` specifies a multiset of letters. Return the number of starting positions where a contiguous log segment is a rearrangement of badge. Overlapping matches count separately. Return 0 if badge is longer than log.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n = log.length ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ m = badge.length ≤ 200000.
• The alphabet is exactly the 26 lowercase English letters; character access is constant time. Do not modify either string.

Examples:
1. log = "ababa", badge = "aab" → 2, at starts 0 and 2.
2. log = "aaaa", badge = "aa" → 3.
3. log = "ab", badge = "abc" → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: The alphabet is exactly the 26 lowercase English letters; character access is constant time. Do not modify either string.

options.text: If m exceeds n return zero. Otherwise build 26 counts for badge and the first length-m segment. Compare the arrays, then replace the outgoing and incoming letters one position at a time, comparing counts and accumulating matches.
options.feedback: A segment is a rearrangement exactly when all 26 multiplicities match. Replacing one letter preserves the counts for the next segment, including overlapping matches.

options.text: For each length-m segment, copy and sort its letters, compare them with a sorted copy of badge, and count matches.
options.feedback: Sorting tests multiset equality correctly, but repeatedly copies and orders letters when counts can be updated between adjacent segments.

options.text: For each length-m segment compare its set of distinct letters with the set for badge. Count equal sets.
options.feedback: For log "abb" and badge "aab", the sets are equal but multiplicities differ; there is no match.

options.text: Use matching letter counts but advance the start by m whenever a match is found, counting only those visited starts.
options.feedback: Overlaps count. For log "aaa" and badge "aa", starts 0 and 1 both match, but jumping by two misses the second.

feedback.reason: An occurrence is a length-m window whose 26 multiplicities all match.
details: Return zero immediately if m exceeds n. Otherwise build two 26-slot arrays for badge and the first m characters of log. Compare all slots for each candidate. Slide by decrementing the outgoing letter and incrementing the incoming letter; count matches without copying strings.

An occurrence is a length-m window whose 26 multiplicities all match. Equal sets of letters are insufficient when repetitions differ. If m>n, return immediately instead of scanning a badge that cannot fit.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Compare counts in consecutive candidate segments” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.
Include the early-return branch m > n. Express the bound over n and m; use n + 1 to cover n = 0.

options.text: O(n + m) time, O(m) auxiliary space
O(nm log(m + 1) + 1) time, O(m) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Compare a fixed 26-counter state per candidate window.
details: The early return handles m > n without reading badge. Otherwise initialization reads m characters and each of n - m + 1 candidates compares exactly 26 slots. Since m ≤ n on this branch, worst-case time is O(n + 1), including the empty-log case, and the arrays occupy fixed space. Array equality checks every multiplicity.
“O(n + m) time, O(m) auxiliary space”: When m>n the fixed method returns without reading badge; otherwise m<=n and two 26-counter arrays have fixed size, not m entries.
“O(nm log(m + 1) + 1) time, O(m) auxiliary space”: This method compares counters, not sorted window copies; no character window is copied or comparison-sorted.
“O(nm + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Each complete window compares exactly 26 counters, so multiplying by badge length m overcounts the fixed work.
